body:
## Summary

`gdoc suggest` replaces matched text as a Google Docs suggestion by deleting the range and inserting the replacement. The inserted text took its style from the character before the insertion point rather than from the text being replaced, so replacing a plain word after a bold code-styled run produced a bold Courier suggestion.

This change preserves the replaced target's direct text style:

- `_replacement_text_style()` in `gdoc/api/docs.py` inspects the body read alongside the matches (including table cells). When every text run overlapping the target shares one `textStyle`, it returns that style plus the set of fields that differ from the neighbouring runs, so those fields are reset explicitly.
- `_build_replacement_requests()` inserts an `updateTextStyle` request over exactly the inserted UTF-16 range after the `insertText`, before any Markdown-driven styling. Explicit replacement Markdown (for example `**bold**`) still overrides the baseline because it is applied afterwards.
- Mixed-style targets, zero-width targets, and targets whose style equals the neighbours' keep the existing behaviour (no extra request).
- `suggest_replacement()` gains an optional `style_body` argument; `cmd_suggest` passes the search body from the same read so no additional API call is made.

Tests: `tests/test_suggest.py` adds parametrised cases covering empty and rich target styles, plain, bold-Markdown, and non-BMP replacements, plus a CLI test asserting the body is threaded through. The full suite (1,570 tests) and `scripts/check-no-stubs.sh` pass.
title: fix: preserve direct target styles in suggested replacements
